root_causes.description: The cart service is the dominant anomaly: its container working set averages ~93MB (peaking ~108MB), roughly 4x peer services (~24MB for product-catalog and checkout), while CPU and error rate remain low. The memory pressure coincides with a p99 latency spike and container recreation/restarts, matching a memory_stress fault.

evidence.observed_value: p99 latency spike max=78.573 ms, anomaly window [1789545942.954→1789545972.954]
cart container recreated/started twice during window (Created count=2, Started count=2)
evidence.expected_baseline: no container recreation during steady state

root_causes.description: Secondary hypothesis: cart's p99 server latency spiked within the incident window, plausibly a downstream symptom of memory pressure/GC rather than an independent fault. Error rate stayed at zero, so this is a latency-dominated signal.

evidence.observed_value: p99 max=78.573 ms, anomaly detected in early window

root_causes.description: Weakest hypothesis: whether the container recreation was accompanied by an OOMKill was not directly observed (no OOMKilled event returned, error rate and error logs were empty), so a pure pod_crash classification is not supported.

evidence.expected_baseline: no error logs in healthy operation

remediation_steps: Disable the cart memory_stress fault via the fault-injection control plane (flagd) for the seed42 scenario.
Inspect and raise the cart pod memory limits/requests, and investigate a possible memory leak — the cart working set (~93-108MB) ran ~4x its peer services.
Monitor cart p99 latency and restart counts after the fault is disabled to confirm recovery.
